issues.description: The problem specification and UML require a public method checkOrderReady() with no parameters. The solution implementation defines checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) and orderMeal calls checkOrderReady(true). This parameter mismatch deviates from the specified API and can confuse students about the required method signature and how orderMeal should invoke it.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature with the problem specification by removing the boolean parameter. Change the solution so checkOrderReady() has no parameters and adjust orderMeal to call checkOrderReady() with no arguments. If the logging behavior is needed for debugging, implement it via an internal flag or a separate private method so the public API matches the spec.

issues.description: The problem specification declares a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void, but the solution implements checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) (a different signature). This mismatch in the expected method signature creates a mapping confusion: students implementing the exercise per the problem will look for/implement a no-arg checkOrderReady(), while the reference solution uses a boolean parameter. The added parameter is not mentioned in the problem or template and may lead students to wonder whether the parameter is required or how to replicate the solution behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature with the problem statement by providing a no-argument checkOrderReady() method in the solution and have orderMeal() call checkOrderReady(). If logging control is needed, use an internal flag or separate private/logging helper so the publicly specified API matches the problem (i.e., public void checkOrderReady()).
